question: Should OpenClaw add a generic adaptive inbound debounce contract, keep fixed debounce as the supported baseline, or defer smarter timing to a plugin/SDK ingress seam?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes how inbound fragments become agent turns, so automation cannot safely choose increment/max, count-trigger, typing-aware, default, and migration semantics.

options.title: Design generic adaptive debounce
options.body: Add one opt-in shared policy with schema/docs/tests for increment, cap, and any selected count or typing signal behavior while preserving current defaults.

options.title: Keep fixed debounce baseline
options.body: Document messages.inbound.debounceMs and queue modes as the supported answer and close or narrow adaptive variants.

options.title: Require plugin or SDK seam first
options.body: Defer the feature until channel plugins can implement smarter ingress timing without growing core message config.

recommendation.title: Design generic adaptive debounce
recommendation.body: Add one opt-in shared policy with schema/docs/tests for increment, cap, and any selected count or typing signal behavior while preserving current defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across shared inbound debounce policy, per-channel config, and ordering fixes.
